_comment: Every address the launch needs, in one place. Nothing here is a secret — these are all
public on chain the moment anything is deployed. The RPC key is deliberately NOT here:
it belongs behind /api/rpc as a server-side environment variable, because anything this
file contains ends up in the repo and anything the page contains ends up in view-source.
_owner: The only address that may deploy, and where every fee goes. Immutable everywhere it appears.

fees._note: snoozeDev only receives anything if devBps > 0, and above zero supplyOnlyFalls() returns false.

token.name: Snooze Bear
token._supply: 1e35 base units = 100 QUADRILLION whole tokens. It is a units choice and NOTHING ELSE: price is E/T, so raising supply lowers the unit price and changes nobody's share of the token. It does not make the token harder to accumulate — curve.virtualEth is the only dial that does, and its comment has the arithmetic. What a high supply does buy is that floor-division dust in the cap and in any future claim is proportionally smaller, and that a buyer's balance reads as a number rather than a decimal. The hard ceiling is the uint192 Rule 2 baseline at ~6.3e57 base units, 22 orders of magnitude above this.
token._devBps: 0 keeps 'supply only falls' exactly true. Up to 2000 is a share OF THE HAIRCUT, never of the trade.
token._dev: What goes in the constructor's `_dev`, which is NOT the same field as fees.snoozeDev. At devBps 0 the dev is paid nothing ever, and LAUNCH.md 3 asks for the zero address here so that anybody reading dev() on chain can see that at a glance — a live-looking address with no cut invites the question. Set this to fees.snoozeDev only if devBps goes above zero; the scripts refuse the combination of a non-zero devBps and a zero dev.

_virtualEth: THE ONLY DIAL THAT MAKES EARLY ACCUMULATION EXPENSIVE, and it is not the supply.
A single buy of R ETH takes exactly R/(E0+R) of everything the curve will ever sell —
the token side cancels, so the answer depends on E0 and on nothing else. At the old
E0 of 3 ETH one buyer with 1 ETH took a quarter of the float in one transaction. At 10:
The cost is graduation: bonding at multiple m needs E0*(sqrt(m)-1) of REAL ETH, so a
curve that is hard to corner is also one that takes longer to bond. There is no setting
that is both. 10 ETH is the middle: a whale needs 5 ETH to reach a third of the float,
and the curve bonds at 21.6 ETH of real buys.
It is also what a buy moves: at 10e18 a 0.1 ETH buy raises the ETH reserve 1.0% and the
PRICE 2.0% — price is E/T, both sides move, so the price change is about double.
curve._bondTarget: E0*(sqrt(m)-1), the REAL ETH that has to arrive before anyone can call bond(). At E0=10 and m=10 that is 21.6228 ETH. Lower it and the curve graduates sooner at a smaller multiple; m=4 would be E0 exactly, 10 ETH.
curve._feeBps: 1%, charged in ETH on the way in and the way out, and paid straight to curveFeeTo. Capped at 500 by the contract.
curve._curveSupply: What the curve may sell — 80% of supply. Not the total supply, and the curve never holds the rest. bondPreview()'s leftover is curveSupply/m, so at the m=10 this bondTarget encodes, 8e33 base units (8% of supply) come back to curveFeeTo when it graduates. The other 20% sits in the owner's wallet from block one, under both rules exactly like anybody else's.

gate._comment: Hold SNOOZE to bid on LAPTOP during the early window. Zero on the SNOOZE curve itself, since there is nothing to hold yet — and both halves have to be zero together, or the constructor reverts.

_comment: The one address on the token that nobody can change afterwards, including you. There is
no oracle in this repository, so there is no default here and the scripts refuse to build
the token transaction while `choice` is empty. Guessing on your behalf would mean shipping
one of the two failures below without anybody having decided to.
SETTABLE is contracts/test/SnoozeMocks.sol:MockOracle — a dial that sets every sale's burn
to anything up to the 90% cap, held forever by whoever holds its key. It must never reach
Base, so deploy/scripts refuses it by comparing deployed bytecode, not by asking.
REVERTING is a permanent honeypot: ready() runs inside every sell, so sells revert while
buys work, and the address cannot be changed. Step 1 calls all three views before the
token exists, which is the only moment refusing still costs nothing.

_choices.observational: A real, ownerless observation on Base — a V3/Slipstream observe() adapter wrapped in try/catch, or a V2-style cumulative-price adapter you checkpoint. Rule 1 starts working once 24h of history exists. LAUNCH.md 2.1 has what it must satisfy.
_choices.never-ready: A deployed oracle whose ready() is false forever. Legitimate, and it means RULE 1 NEVER FIRES: no sale is ever haircut, at any price, on any day. $SNOOZE is then an ordinary ERC-20 with a 20%/day cap on selling into the curve, and nothing else. deploy/deploy.html says exactly that on its face when this is the choice, rather than in a comment.

oracle._address: Where the chosen oracle is deployed. Step 1 checks ready(), spot() and twap24() all return without reverting WITH NO HISTORY YET, because that is the state they will be in at the moment of launch.

vanity._comment: An address is hex, so only 0-9 and a-f exist in one. PUMP, DUMP, BULL, MOON, BEAR and ZZZ all contain letters the alphabet does not have and cannot be ground at any cost.
vanity._reachable: ba5ed (BASED), bada55 (BADASS), 1337 (LEET), 600d (GOOD), beabed (BEA-BED), 5eeded (SEEDED), acce55 (ACCESS), f00d, face, dead, cafe, beef
vanity._ifYouWantAWordThatIsNotHex: It goes in a Base name, not in the address. pump.snoozebear.eth is what a wallet shows people; the hex underneath it can be anything.
_suffix: 8453 is Base's chain id, and every character of it is a digit, so unlike BASE it is
reachable. Four hex characters is 16^4 = 65,536 salts on average, which is about a
second — cheap enough that a re-grind after a missed prediction costs nothing.
Rejected: ba5ed (BASED), the previous value, at 16^5 = 1.05M and about seven seconds.
Nothing wrong with it; 8453 says the chain rather than a pun, and a chain id is the one
thing a buyer checking an address on a block explorer is actually looking for.
Rejected: both, ...ba5ed8453. Nine characters is 16^9 = 68.7 BILLION salts, and this
machine grinds about 150k/s across its lanes, so five days — for an address nobody
reads past the first six characters of anyway.
_target: Which contract gets the ground address. It is NOT the token, and that is a fact about
these contracts rather than a preference:
Snooze's constructor runs `balanceOf[msg.sender] = supply` and `admin = msg.sender`.
Deployed through SnoozeDeployer, msg.sender is the DEPLOYER CONTRACT — so the entire
supply is minted to a contract with no transfer, no approve and no rescue, and the admin
that could register the curve as a pool is that same contract, which has no function that
could call setPool. The supply would be unrecoverable and neither Snooze rule could ever
be switched on. test/run-deploy.mjs deploys it that way and measures both.
So the token is deployed from the owner's wallet, and the ground address goes to the
curve — which is the address buyers actually send ETH to, takes nothing from msg.sender,
and has no admin at all. "token" is refused.
vanity._grind: node deploy/scripts/grind.mjs   (which computes the real init-code hash first, then runs tools/vanity-par.mjs)
vanity._warning: The address depends on the exact bytecode AND the constructor arguments. The curve's arguments contain the token address, so this cannot even be attempted before the token exists. Grind last.
